transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name], and I'll be speaking with you today. Can you tell me what brings you in to see me?

Honestly, I'm here because... well, HR at work and my sister keep saying I've gotten too thin. Which is ridiculous. My sister, she's always been a worrier, always on my case about something, especially since the divorce. The divorce was just... a whole nightmare, honestly. She took the house, which, fine, but she also took the espresso machine I bought in Italy. Can you believe that? I dragged that heavy thing on a plane. 

But anyway, yeah, my weight has kept dropping since the divorce, but from my side, I just see that my suits fit sharper. I'm in wholesale sales, manufacturing equipment, so you have to look good, you know? First impressions and all that. I actually had to take a bunch of my jackets to this tailor downtown—Tony, great guy, his shop has been there for like thirty years—to get them taken in. He did an incredible job on the shoulders. But yeah, my sister and HR wouldn't drop it, so they told me I needed to come see someone. So here I am.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or social activities?

I mean, I still manage my sales route perfectly fine. Actually, I was just up in Albany on Tuesday—beautiful drive, honestly, the leaves are just starting to change. Though the traffic on I-87 was an absolute joke. They've been doing construction near exit 12 for what feels like a decade, I swear, just cones everywhere and nobody actually working. 

But anyway, work is good. Socially... I guess I have been keeping to myself a bit more lately. Turning down invitations and stuff. It's just... I avoid client dinners now, and dates too, honestly, unless I can completely control the menu. You know how it is with these restaurants people always want to go to. Like, my biggest client always wants to go to this old-school steakhouse downtown, and the waiters there are so pushy about ordering all these family-style sides, and everything is just drowning in butter and oil. It's too much of a hassle to deal with. So yeah, I just make excuses and skip them now. It's easier to just stay in.
Have you felt less pleasure or interest in activities that you used to enjoy, even things you looked forward to?

I mean, no, not really. I still like the stuff I always liked. Like, I still love golf, for instance. I haven't been playing as much this season, but that's mostly because my usual golf buddy was my ex-wife's brother, Dan. And obviously, after the whole divorce thing, that got super awkward. Which is a real shame, honestly, because we used to play at this great course out in the suburbs—Oak Ridge, I don't know if you've ever been? Beautiful greens, but their sand traps are just absolutely brutal. I swear I spent half of last summer just trying to get out of the bunker on the 14th hole. Dan actually snapped his pitching wedge in half on a tree root there once, just completely lost his temper. It was hilarious. 

But yeah, anyway, I still enjoy things just fine. It's just... you know, circumstances change who you can hang out with.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, even if just for a short period?

Not really, no. I mean, I wouldn't say I'm sad or hopeless. The divorce was rough, sure, but I'm moving on. I actually just bought a new couch for my apartment. The old one was this hideous floral pattern my ex insisted on—she got it at some estate sale in Connecticut and was obsessed with it, but it was like sitting on a pile of rocks. So I finally went to that big furniture place out on Route 4. You know the one with the massive red sign? I spent like three hours in there. The salesman, Jerry, he was a real character. Kept trying to upsell me on this leather sectional that was basically the size of a minivan. I told him, Jerry, I live in a two-bedroom apartment, I'm not outfitting a movie theater. But yeah, I ended up with a really nice, clean-lined gray sofa. Much better. But anyway, what were you asking? Oh, feeling down. No, I feel fine. Just focused on work and getting the apartment set up.
Have you been deliberately restricting your food intake, watching what you eat closely, or changing your eating habits because of concerns about your weight or shape?

I mean, I guess I'm careful. I have to be, you know? With the driving and the sitting all day. Most days I just stick to coffee in the morning. I get it from this little drive-thru place near my apartment—Beans and Leaves, I think it's called? The girl who works the window, Sarah, she's always there, every single morning. I don't know when she sleeps. She makes this amazing cold brew, though. It's so strong it'll strip the paint off a car, but it gets me going. 

So yeah, just coffee, and then maybe a protein bar if I'm stuck between sales calls. I actually found these new ones at the gas station, they're supposed to taste like birthday cake, but honestly, it's more like chewing on flavored cardboard. Still, it does the job. And then at night, I'll just have something small, like... just some grilled chicken. No rice, no sides. Because honestly, if I sit down and eat a whole, heavy meal, it just feels like I ruined the whole day. Like I just threw away all that discipline, you know? Plus, eating heavy at night just messes with my sleep, and I need to be sharp for my morning calls. My manager, Dave, he's been on this whole kick lately about morning check-ins at 7:30 AM. Who does that? It's absurd. But yeah, I just keep it light.
Do you have a strong fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even when you're at a normal weight or underweight?

I mean, yeah, I guess I do worry about it. It's like... if I have to take a client out for dinner, or like last month when I went to Miami for a weekend—which, by the way, Miami is just out of control right now. The traffic down there? Unbelievable. I rented this little convertible, thought it would be fun, right? Cruise down Ocean Drive. But I spent the whole time just sitting bumper-to-bumper behind these massive party buses. And the humidity just destroys the leather seats in those rentals. I don't know how people live down there year-round. My buddy Mark moved to Boca a few years ago, and he says you just get used to sweating 24/7, but I don't know. 

But anyway, yeah, if I go out like that and I come back and the scale is even a pound higher, I get this... this massive panic. It feels like I'm completely losing control of everything. And right away, I'm just in my head, planning exactly how I'm going to cut back the next day to fix it. It just completely ruins my mood until the number goes back down.
Do you currently see yourself as overweight or gaining weight, even if others might say you look thin or underweight?

I don't know about overweight, exactly, but... I definitely don't see what other people say they see. Like, when I look in the mirror, especially if I'm getting ready for a big client meeting or, I don't know, a date—which I haven't really been doing much of since the divorce. I actually tried one of those dating apps a few weeks ago. The one where you have to answer all those weird prompts? I spent like an hour trying to come up with a funny answer to "my most controversial opinion." I ended up putting something about how deep-dish pizza is just a casserole, which I stand by, by the way. I mean, it's good, but it's not pizza. Anyway, I went on one date with this woman who worked in marketing, and we went to this tapas place downtown. The parking was a nightmare. I had to park like six blocks away in this garage that charged twenty dollars an hour. Who carries that kind of cash? I had to use an ATM that charged me a four-dollar fee. It's basically robbery. 

But yeah, when I'm getting dressed for something like that, I just zero right in on my stomach and my face. And if I look in the mirror and I think I look even a little bit soft, or if my jawline isn't sharp, I just feel... I feel like everyone is going to look at me and think I'm sloppy. Or weak, you know? Like I don't have my life together. In sales, you have to look sharp, you have to look hungry. If you look soft, people just don't respect you the same way.
Has your concern about your weight or shape ever caused problems in your relationships, work, or other important areas of your life?

I mean, I still manage my sales route fine. I hit my numbers. But... yeah, I guess it's changed things. Like, I avoid client dinners now unless I know exactly where we're going and I can control the menu. Which is tough, because in my industry, taking a client out to a nice steakhouse is basically how you close a deal. I had this one guy, Greg, runs a huge distribution center out in Ohio. He always wants to go to this specific Italian place when he's in town. Mamma Rosa's or something. The portions there are just... they're comical. They bring out a bowl of pasta that could feed a family of four, and it's swimming in oil. And they have this garlic bread that they just keep bringing to the table, basket after basket. I don't know how they make money on it, honestly. It's like they're just trying to see how much bread one human being can consume. 

So yeah, I've just been turning down invitations like that. I tell them I have a conflict, or I try to switch it to a morning coffee meeting instead. And dating, like I said, I just don't really do it right now unless we can just get a drink or something. It's just easier to keep to myself. I don't have to explain why I'm not eating the bread or why I'm ordering a dry salad. It's just... less exhausting to be alone, you know?
When you say you've been careful with food and avoid eating heavy meals, is that mainly to keep your weight down, and does the idea of gaining any weight feel unacceptable to you?

I mean, I don't know if I'd use the word unacceptable, exactly. I'm not really sure I think about it like that. It's more just... I like to keep things tight, you know? If you eat those heavy meals, you just get so slow and sluggish. Like, last Tuesday, I had to drive up to Albany for a pitch with a new supplier. Have you driven up I-87 lately? The construction up there is just an absolute nightmare. They've had this one lane closed near Kingston for what feels like six months now. Just miles of orange cones, and you look over and nobody is actually working. I swear I saw one guy just leaning on a backhoe, scrolling on his phone and drinking a Dunkin' iced coffee. 

Which, by the way, have you tried using their new paper straws? They dissolve in like two minutes. You can't even finish a medium cold brew before you're just chewing on wet cardboard. It's ridiculous. I ended up spilling half of it on my slacks because the lid popped off when I hit a massive pothole right outside of Newburgh. Had to stop at a rest area and try to scrub it out with those terrible brown paper towels they have in public bathrooms. 

But yeah, I don't know. I haven't really noticed if it's specifically about the weight being unacceptable. I just... I don't like feeling bogged down.
Do you ever engage in behaviors like excessive exercise, fasting, or making yourself vomit to compensate for eating something you consider unhealthy or to control your weight?

I don't really do any of that, no. I mean, I run, but just normal running. I've got this trail near my apartment, actually, it goes right along the river. It's really nice in the mornings before the humidity hits. Though lately, they've had all these people riding those electric scooters on it. Have you seen those things? They just leave them everywhere. Like, right in the middle of the sidewalk, or tipped over in the grass. I saw one thrown into the bushes outside my building last week. It's like, who is paying for these? And they go so fast, too. You're just trying to get a couple miles in, and suddenly some college kid in flip-flops comes flying past you at twenty miles an hour. It's a hazard, honestly. 

But no, I don't... I don't do the fasting thing or making myself sick or anything like that. I just try to be careful, you know? Keep a handle on things.
Do you find that your overall sense of how you’re doing in life, or how you feel about yourself, is strongly influenced by your weight or how you feel you look?

Yeah, I guess it is. I mean, when I look in the mirror before a meeting or, you know, if I'm actually going on a date, I just immediately zero in on my stomach and my face. If I think I look soft or bloated, I just feel like everyone is going to see me as sloppy or weak. Like I don't have my life together. 

Which is crazy because in sales, perception is everything. You have to look sharp. I actually just bought this new suit from a guy downtown. He's one of those old-school tailors, been in the same shop since the eighties. Still uses chalk and a tape measure around his neck. The shop smells like mothballs and stale coffee, but the guy is a genius. He was telling me about how the fabric industry has completely changed since the pandemic. Apparently, getting good Italian wool is a nightmare now because of supply chain issues. Ships just sitting in ports for weeks. It makes you wonder how anything gets done anymore, honestly. Like, if you can't even get a roll of fabric across the ocean without a massive delay, how does the global economy even function? 

But yeah, if I don't look sharp, if I feel like I'm carrying extra weight in my face, I just feel off my game. Like I can't close the deal.

They bring out a bowl of pasta that could feed a family of four, and it's swimming in oil. And they have this garlic bread that they just keep bringing to the table, basket after basket. I don't know how they make money on it, honestly. It's like they're just trying to see how much bread one human being can consume. 

So yeah, I've just been turning down invitations like that. I tell them I have a conflict, or I try to switch it to a morning coffee meeting instead. And dating, like I said, I just don't really do it right now unless we can just get a drink or something. It's just easier to keep to myself. I don't have to explain why I'm not eating the bread or why I'm ordering a dry salad. It's just... less exhausting to be alone, you know?

patient.answer:
Yeah, I guess it is. I mean, when I look in the mirror before a meeting or, you know, if I'm actually going on a date, I just immediately zero in on my stomach and my face. If I think I look soft or bloated, I just feel like everyone is going to see me as sloppy or weak. Like I don't have my life together. 

Which is crazy because in sales, perception is everything. You have to look sharp. I actually just bought this new suit from a guy downtown. He's one of those old-school tailors, been in the same shop since the eighties. Still uses chalk and a tape measure around his neck. The shop smells like mothballs and stale coffee, but the guy is a genius. He was telling me about how the fabric industry has completely changed since the pandemic. Apparently, getting good Italian wool is a nightmare now because of supply chain issues. Ships just sitting in ports for weeks. It makes you wonder how anything gets done anymore, honestly. Like, if you can't even get a roll of fabric across the ocean without a massive delay, how does the global economy even function? 

But yeah, if I don't look sharp, if I feel like I'm carrying extra weight in my face, I just feel off my game. Like I can't close the deal.
